claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Combining hierarchical microstructural features with compositional descriptors in an ML framework can accurately predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed ML framework will dramatically reduce computational expense.
Grain-size distributions, chemical-fluctuation spatial statistics, and phase fractions are informative features for predicting the specified mechanical properties.
A model trained on comparable multi-principal-element and high-entropy alloys can generalize to HfNbTiVAl10.
The predictions are applicable to standardized tensile and fracture testing at room temperature and conventional strain rates.
Preservation of the hierarchical heterostructure is required for the model to remain applicable.
The multiscale hierarchical heterostructure, including chemical fluctuations and phase heterogeneity, mediates stress distribution, yielding, and crack propagation.
Localized chemical ordering and grain-boundary networks dominate the mechanical response sufficiently to encode the underlying deformation and fracture mechanisms.
Encoding these microstructural characteristics permits accurate mechanical-property prediction without computationally intensive first-principles or exhaustive CALPHAD calculations.
Predicted Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness will each be within ±10–15% of experimental values.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by at least one order of magnitude relative to full-scale first-principles or phase-diagram approaches.
Thermophysical-parameter calculations, CALPHAD, and high-fidelity first-principles simulations require vast computational resources.
Prior thermophysical, CALPHAD, and first-principles methods have limited accuracy, particularly for fracture and toughness.
The model may become unreliable when processing produces hierarchical microstructures outside the training-data distribution.
The model may become unreliable if characterization omits microstructural features needed by the feature-extraction pipeline.
Preliminary evidence suggests that feature-based ML can improve predictive efficiency and accuracy.
The exact error margins and computational savings remain uncertain until validation on a statistically significant HfNbTiVAl10 sample set.
